name: Netskope applicant-stage disclosure

attribution.legal_posture: Company-specific applicant observation attributed by The Register to Netskope's CISO in an original interview and reported in The Register's canonical original interview article; it is a company interview observation, rather than a first-party company page or a definitive DPRK determination for every fraudulent applicant.

caveats: Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, remote-work preference, camera behavior, VPN use, and any single device, network, phone, or account-age signal require corroboration before attribution.

Fraudulent applicants require individual evidence before classification as DPRK-linked.
The source describes an attempted scenario; hire and compromise outcomes remain unresolved.
In-person onboarding or address checking requires accessibility, privacy, labor, and legal review before any general policy.
This record covers aggregate context; applicant, worker, identity-theft victim, current account, private customer, and anonymized legal-entity identity require separate evidence.

statements: Netskope's CISO said the company received fraudulent-worker applications and adapted screening and onboarding after identifying copied or synthetic-looking profiles.
Reported outcome: Fraudulent applicants detected; some withdrew under stronger controls; no hire or access reported.
limitations: Do not classify every fraudulent applicant as DPRK-linked.
Do not infer a successful hire or compromise.
Do not turn in-person onboarding or address checking into universal policy without accessibility, privacy, labor, and legal review.
Applicant-stage reporting does not establish a successful hire, system access, post-hire conduct, or harm unless the cited source expressly says so.
No applicant, worker, identity-theft victim, current account, private customer, or anonymized legal entity may be identified or inferred from this record.

Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, remote-work preference, camera behavior, VPN use, or any single device, network, phone, or account-age signal is not attribution evidence by itself.

sources.support: Canonical-source boundary: the cited URL is The Register's verified original article; the company statements remain reported executive observations, not first-party company pages or adjudicated findings. Snowflake CISO Brad Jones told the publication that Snowflake had seen applicants fitting the DPRK-linked category and had shared associated indicators with peers. Netskope CISO James Robinson said Netskope had received fraudulent-worker applications; he described resumes apparently built from stolen or fake identities, an FBI briefing involving security, HR and legal, recruiter detection of copied profiles, and applicants withdrawing when stronger onboarding checks were required. Normalized boundary: Netskope's CISO said the company received fraudulent-worker applications and adapted screening and onboarding after identifying copied or synthetic-looking profiles. Attribution boundary: Named executives' original company-specific applicant observations as reported by a reputable technology publication. The article does not establish a successful hire or definitive legal identity for any applicant. Publication boundary: Create at most separate applicant-stage organization disclosures for Snowflake and Netskope. Do not retain the article's example candidate names, contact fields, or indicator values
